facts.text: Bridgton was organized in 1779 as Bridgetown Plantation, named after Moody Bridges, and incorporated on February 7, 1794.
In the 19th century Bridgton grew into an industrial hub with sawmills, gristmills, woolen textile mills, a tannery, shoe factory and brick manufacturer.
When the main line bypassed Bridgton, the town built a 2‑foot‑gauge Bridgton and Saco River Railroad in 1883 to connect to the national network.
The Bridgton Historical Society preserves 250 years of local history in a museum on Main Street, offering permanent exhibitions and a collection of over 2,000 works.
Bridgton Academy, a private preparatory school, is a long‑standing institution in the town.
Pleasant Mountain Ski Area, formerly Shawnee Peak, sits in Bridgton’s western hills and draws skiers from across Maine.
